No Water Added Pumpkin Soup · Part Two

Whole chicken version · 350°F · About 3 hours

The pumpkin doubles as the cooking pot. The chicken and vegetables release their juices as they bake, and miso rubbed inside the pumpkin gives the broth a savory base.

Ingredients and method

Ingredients

  • 1 extra-large pumpkin
  • 1 whole chicken
  • ½ cabbage
  • 1 onion
  • 1 handful of small tomatoes
  • 2 bell peppers
  • Fresh ginger and garlic
  • Miso paste
  • Old Bay seasoning
  • Jamaican jerk seasoning
  • ½ packet SpiCity seasoning

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 350°F. Cut a lid from the top of the pumpkin, scoop out the seeds and strings, and rub miso paste over the inside.
  2. Season the chicken with Old Bay and Jamaican jerk seasoning.
  3. Layer some of the cabbage and onion in the bottom of the pumpkin. Set the chicken on top and add the remaining cabbage and onion, tomatoes, bell peppers, ginger, garlic, and SpiCity seasoning. The chicken and vegetables provide the liquid as they cook.
  4. Bake for about 3 hours. Check with a food thermometer that the chicken reaches 165°F in the thickest part of the breast and the innermost parts of the thigh and wing. Check that the vegetables and broth inside the pumpkin also reach 165°F before serving.

West African Potato Greens

Buy recipe PDF · $4

Sweet potato leaves with steak, chicken, and bell pepper. I like my greens cut very fine, bright green, and still a little crunchy.

Serves about 4

Ingredients and method

Ingredients

  • 1 pound trimmed sweet potato leaves
  • 1 onion and 1 bell pepper, green or red
  • Equal parts steak and chicken. Dried fish is optional.
  • All-purpose seasoning, spicy chili crisp, a little lemon juice, and salt for the meat
  • 1½ tablespoons olive oil for the pan
  • A little all-purpose seasoning and optional Maggi or chicken bouillon for the greens
  • Cooked rice, for serving

Method

  1. Rinse and drain the sweet potato leaves. Chop them very finely.
  2. Season the steak and chicken with all-purpose seasoning, chili crisp, lemon juice, and salt. Steam or boil until cooked through, or air-fry the chicken. Drain any excess liquid and set aside.
  3. Warm the olive oil in a pan. Add the greens directly to the oil and immediately layer the onion and bell pepper on top. Sprinkle with a little all-purpose seasoning and optional Maggi or chicken bouillon.
  4. Add the cooked steak and chicken while the vegetables steam. Steam for a few minutes, then stir gently. Use as little liquid as possible so the leaves stay bright and slightly crisp. Serve with rice.

From My Kitchen

African Spinach with Shrimp

Buy recipe PDF · $4

The same layering method, with smoky shrimp, sweet bell pepper, and a little lime.

Serves about 4

Ingredients and method

Ingredients

  • 1 pound trimmed African spinach
  • 1 onion and 1 bell pepper, green or red
  • 1 pound peeled, deveined shrimp
  • 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, ½ teaspoon garlic powder, ¼ teaspoon ground black pepper, and the zest of ½ lime
  • A pinch of cayenne and salt, optional
  • 1½ tablespoons olive oil for the pan
  • A little all-purpose seasoning and optional Maggi or chicken bouillon for the greens
  • Cooked rice, for serving

Method

  1. Rinse and drain the spinach well, then chop it finely.
  2. Pat the shrimp dry and toss with the smoked paprika, garlic powder, black pepper, and lime zest. Add cayenne and salt if using. Cook the shrimp separately, drain any excess liquid, and set aside.
  3. Warm the olive oil in a pan. Add the spinach and immediately layer the onion and bell pepper on top. Sprinkle with a little all-purpose seasoning and optional Maggi or chicken bouillon.
  4. Add the cooked shrimp while the vegetables steam. Let everything steam together briefly, then stir gently. The greens should still have a little bite. Serve with rice.

Pineapple Cucumber Juice with Ginger and Lime

Sweet pineapple and cool cucumber make a refreshing juice with tart lime and a little kick from fresh ginger.

Ingredients and method

Ingredients

  • 1 medium pineapple
  • 1 medium cucumber
  • 1 medium lime
  • ½-inch piece of fresh ginger

Method

  1. Peel the pineapple and lime. Wash the cucumber and ginger. Cut the produce as needed to fit your juicer.
  2. Run everything through the juicer. Stir and serve chilled or over ice.

Beet, Orange & Apple Juice with Ginger

A ruby-red, naturally caffeine-free juice with earthy beets, bright orange, sweet apple, and a kick from fresh ginger.

Serving suggestion: a small glass (about 5 fl oz) with a meal.

Ingredients and method

Ingredients

  • 2 beets
  • 3 oranges
  • 3 apples
  • ½-inch piece of fresh ginger

Method

  1. Scrub the beets, wash the apples and ginger, and peel the oranges. Trim the beets, remove the apple cores, and cut the produce to fit your juicer.
  2. Run everything through the juicer. Stir and serve chilled or over ice.
Cook Along ↗

Carrot, Green Apple & Lime Juice

Sweet carrots, tart green apples, and fresh lime make a bright, crisp juice.

Ingredients and method

Ingredients

  • 3 carrots
  • 2 green apples
  • 1 lime

Method

  1. Scrub and trim the carrots, wash and core the apples, and peel the lime. Cut everything to fit your juicer.
  2. Run all three ingredients through the juicer. Stir and serve chilled or over ice.
